title: I was sent to perfect character
hook: the Prophet ﷺ said he was sent to perfect good character

segments.voice: Yesterday, the theology close, and your line: believe, and live it. Did you move one obstacle out of someone's way? Today a new block begins: the inward path and good character. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-eight.

Ask a room why a prophet is sent, and the answers come fast. To bring a law. To call people to worship one God. To warn, to give good news. All of those are in the Qur'an. But there's a hadith where the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sums up his mission in a way that can catch a listener off guard. Not with law, not with ritual. With character. Today's word is the Arabic for it.
screen: `WHY IS A PROPHET SENT?` → `LAW, WORSHIP, WARNING.` → `AND THEN: CHARACTER.`

segments.voice: The word is akhlaq: character, manners, the settled habits of a person, how they are when nobody's grading them. The hadith comes in Imam Malik's Muwatta, among other collections, and in paraphrase it says: I was sent to perfect good character. Imam Ahmad's collection has a version that says noble character. Notice the verb. Perfect. Complete. Not invent. Some readers take it to mean that good character, honesty, generosity, keeping a promise, was already known, and the Prophet came to bring it to completion. The Qur'an says something about his own. Addressing him, it says, in Pickthall's translation: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." Tremendous. And when his wife Aisha was asked to describe his character, her answer in Sahih Muslim is short: his character was the Qur'an. In other words, what the book says, he was. So this block opens with a turn. The last block asked what Muslims believe. This one asks what kind of person belief makes. Muslim scholars wrote whole works on akhlaq: on patience and anger, on envy and generosity, on the heart's diseases and cures. Over the coming weeks we'll walk through some of them. And day to day? A hadith in Bukhari puts it plainly: the best of you are those who are best in character. Not the loudest, not the most learned. The best in character. That's a measure anybody can be held to, at a checkout counter, on a crowded train, in a group chat.
screen: `AKHLAQ: WHO YOU ARE UNGRADED.` · `SENT TO PERFECT, NOT TO INVENT.` · `HIS CHARACTER WAS THE QUR'AN.` · then, large: `THE BEST OF YOU: BEST IN CHARACTER.`

segments.voice: The practice: practice one good trait. Settle, and breathe. Pick one trait you'd like to grow today. Patience, honesty, generosity, gentleness, keeping your word. Just one. Now shrink it to something small enough to do before tonight. Honesty might be one true sentence where an easy one would do. Generosity might be letting someone go first. Keeping your word might be the call you said you'd make. Say the small act to yourself, plainly, once. If you pray, you can ask Allah to beautify your character, in your own words. If not, simply set the intention. The bell holds the time.
Akhlaq. Character: the settled habits of a person, which the Prophet said he was sent to perfect. Today's word.
Your line: sent for character. Today, do the small act you chose, on purpose. Tomorrow, al-Ghazali's Revival. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims study akhlaq, good character, as part of the faith, often starting from the hadith that the Prophet was sent to perfect good character and from accounts of his own conduct.
